column2: Wash the potatoes and cut into large slices, peeled or unpeeled.
Trim excess fatty skin from the drumsticks and pat dry with kitchen paper.
Toss the drumsticks and potatoes with the oil, thyme, ground pepper and a little salt.
Bake for 45–55 minutes.
Turn the chicken and vegetables halfway through cooking.
Cut into the thickest part to check: there should be no pink and the juices should run clear; with a thermometer the core should reach at least 74°C.
Remove from the heat or oven and rest for 3–5 minutes; the juices settle back in and it stays juicier.
Cut the chicken into thin strips.
Cut raw chicken on a separate board; then wash the board, knife and your hands with hot soapy water.
Slice the onion and cut the courgette and pepper to the same size as the chicken.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and stir-fry the chicken over high heat for 5–6 minutes until browned.
Add the courgette and cook for 6–8 more minutes, keeping it slightly firm.
Mix the lemon juice, crushed garlic, olive oil, thyme and a little salt.
Butterfly the chicken breast at its thickest part so it is an even thickness.
Coat the chicken well in the marinade; leave in a covered container in the fridge for at least 20 minutes.
Heat the pan over medium heat; add the chicken and cook for 6–8 minutes without moving it.
Turn and cook the other side for 6–8 minutes; add the remaining marinade to the pan for the last 2 minutes.
Put the chicken in a pan with 3 glasses of water and bring to the boil; skim off the foam.
Simmer over low heat for 20–25 minutes until completely white inside.
Take out the chicken and shred it; strain the cooking liquid and set aside 1.5 glasses.
Heat the butter and olive oil in the pan and fry the rice for 3 minutes.
Add the hot chicken stock; when it boils, turn the heat to the lowest setting and cook covered for 12–15 minutes.
Spread the shredded chicken on top; put a clean cloth under the lid and let it rest for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.
Cook the pasta in salted boiling water for the time on the packet; save a ladle of the water and drain.
Heat the oil in the pan and sauté the chicken for 6–7 minutes until white all over.
Add the crushed garlic and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the grated tomato and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the pasta to the sauce; if it is too thick, loosen with the reserved water and toss.
Cut the chicken into 3 cm cubes and the peppers to a similar size.
Mix the yoghurt, oil, thyme and a little salt and coat the chicken; refrigerate for 30 minutes.
If using wooden skewers, soak them in water for 20 minutes so they don't burn in the oven.
Preheat the oven to 200°C. Line a tray with baking paper.
Thread the chicken and peppers alternately onto the skewers without packing too tightly.
Bake for 20–25 minutes, turning the skewers halfway.
Heat half the oil in a pan and sauté the chicken for 8–10 minutes until fully cooked.
Whisk the yoghurt with crushed garlic and a little salt.
Rest the chicken for 3 minutes, transfer to a serving plate and pour the yoghurt over it.
Heat the remaining oil in a small pan and stir in the red pepper for 10 seconds; drizzle over the yoghurt without burning it.
Peel the aubergine in stripes and dice it; soak in salted water for 15 minutes and squeeze.
Cut the potatoes, tomatoes and onion to the same size as the chicken.
Put the chicken and vegetables in the casserole; add the oil, a little salt and the hot water and mix.
Bake for 40 minutes with the lid or foil on.
Uncover and bake for 15 more minutes until lightly browned on top.
Grate the onion and squeeze out the juice; chop the parsley finely.
Knead the chicken mince, egg, breadcrumbs, onion, parsley and a little salt for 2–3 minutes.
Rest the mixture in the fridge for 15 minutes; it will be easier to shape.
With wet hands shape walnut-sized meatballs and arrange them spaced apart on the tray.
Brush the tops lightly with oil.
Bake for 20–25 minutes.
Turn the meatballs halfway through so both sides brown.
Cut the onion and pepper into thin strips.
Heat the oil in the pan and stir-fry the chicken over high heat for 6–7 minutes.
Add the onion and pepper and cook for 4–5 more minutes.
Warm the flatbreads in a dry pan for 20 seconds per side.
Spread yoghurt on the flatbreads, add the chicken mixture, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Cut the chicken into large pieces and the potatoes into 1 cm slices.
Put the chicken and potatoes in the ovenproof dish; toss with the oil, thyme and a little salt.
Bake for 35–45 minutes.
Cut the chicken into small cubes.
Dice the courgette, pepper and onion small on a separate board.
Heat the oil in the pan and stir-fry the chicken over high heat for 5–6 minutes until browned.
Add the onion and pepper and stir for 4 minutes.
Add the courgette and cook for 5–6 minutes until the vegetables are soft.
Wipe the mushrooms with a damp cloth and slice; chop the onion and pepper.
Heat the oil in the pan and sauté the onion and pepper for 4 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for 6–7 minutes until white all over.
Add the mushrooms and cook over high heat for 6–8 minutes until their liquid has evaporated.
Pat the drumsticks dry with kitchen paper.
Cut the potatoes and carrots into large pieces.
Toss the drumsticks and vegetables with the oil, thyme and a little salt.
Spread in the ovenproof dish in a single layer.
Bake for 40–45 minutes.
Mix the lemon juice, oil, crushed garlic, thyme and a little salt.
Pat the drumsticks dry and score them in a few places with a knife so the marinade penetrates.
Arrange the drumsticks in the ovenproof dish and pour the remaining marinade over them.
Bake for 40–45 minutes; turn halfway and baste with the juices in the tray.
Mix the yoghurt, oil, crushed garlic, thyme and a little salt.
Trim excess fat from the chicken thighs and pat dry.
Preheat the oven to 200°C; arrange the chicken in the ovenproof dish, spaced apart.
Bake for 35–40 minutes, turning halfway.
Cut the chicken into bite-sized cubes.
Heat the oil in the pan and sear the chicken over high heat for 3–4 minutes until coloured outside.
Dice the tomatoes and slice the pepper into rings.
Put the chicken, tomatoes and pepper in the ovenproof dish and mix with a little salt.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked.
Scatter the grated cheese and bake for 5 more minutes until melted.
Preheat the oven to 190°C. Line a tray with baking paper.
Finely grate the vegetables and squeeze out the liquid firmly with your hands so the meatballs hold together.
Knead the turkey mince, vegetables, egg, breadcrumbs and a little salt.
Bake for about 25 minutes.
Break one meatball in half to check: there should be no pink inside; with a thermometer it should reach at least 74°C.
Dice the courgette, tomatoes and red pepper.
Put the chicken and vegetables in the ovenproof dish; add the olive oil, a little salt and half a tea glass of water and mix.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for 10 more minutes.
Heat the oil in the pan and fry the onion for 3–4 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir for 5 minutes until white on the outside.
Add the tomato paste and fry for 1 minute; add the tomato and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the chickpeas and 1 glass of hot water; when it boils, lower the heat.
Cook covered for 20 minutes.
Finely grate the courgette and squeeze out the liquid firmly.
Knead the chicken mince, courgette, egg, breadcrumbs and a little salt.
Brush the tops with olive oil.
Pat the wings thoroughly dry with kitchen paper; dry skin crisps better.
Arrange the wings on the tray in a single layer.
Bake for 40–45 minutes, turning every 15 minutes.
Pat the thighs dry; cut the potatoes into large slices.
Mix the oil, thyme, crushed garlic and a little salt.
Toss the thighs and potatoes in this mixture and arrange on the tray in a single layer.
Cut the turkey into large 4–5 cm pieces.
Cut the carrots, courgette and onion into large pieces.
Toss the turkey and vegetables with the oil, thyme and a little salt.
Remove the paper and bake for 10–15 more minutes until lightly browned.
Cut into the thickest piece of turkey to check: there should be no pink; with a thermometer it should reach at least 74°C.
Cut the chicken into 2–3 cm cubes; chop the onion finely.
Wipe the mushrooms with a damp cloth and slice them.
Heat the oil in a wide pan and stir the onion for 2 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir-fry over high heat for 5–6 minutes until browned all over.
Add the mushrooms and stir for 3 minutes until they release their liquid.
Add the hot water; cook covered over medium-low heat for 10–15 minutes until the chicken is fully cooked.
Add the thyme in the last 1–2 minutes and stir through.
Slice the courgette into half-moons.
Add the lemon juice just before taking off the heat and stir.
Slice the red pepper into strips.
Add the pepper and stir for 2 minutes.
Tear the basil leaves by hand and add them after turning off the heat.
Wash the spinach in plenty of water and chop roughly; crush the garlic.
Add the spinach and stir for 2 minutes until wilted.
Add the garlic in the last 1–2 minutes and stir through without burning it.
Break the broccoli into small florets; grate the ginger.
Add the broccoli and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the ginger in the last 1–2 minutes and stir through.
Slice the carrots into thin half-moons.
Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for 1–2 minutes and sprinkle on top when serving.
Slit the leek lengthwise and wash the layers well; slice into thin rings.
Add the leek and stir for 3 minutes.
Loosen the mustard with 2 spoonfuls of the cooking liquid and add it in the last 1–2 minutes.
Dice the tomatoes; slice the olives into rings.
Add the tomato and stir for 3 minutes.
Add the olives in the last 1–2 minutes; since olives are salty, use less salt.
Add the aubergine and stir for 3 minutes.
Add the cumin in the last 1–2 minutes and stir through.
Add the peas and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the dill after turning off the heat and stir.
